cohort: The cohort comprised 311 pregnant women aged 35 or above attending an antenatal clinic and delivering at a tertiary care hospital, excluding those with major pre-existing medical conditions.
finding: Elderly pregnancies were found to carry a greater risk for both maternal and fetal complications, including gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, low birth weight, preterm labor, and an increased likelihood of cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: The study reported that 58.5% of elderly pregnant women had cesarean sections, indicating an increased likelihood of cesarean delivery in this population.
